transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-27 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Accelera Procurement), Samantha Lee (Accelera Legal), Raj Patel (Accelera CTO)

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick note, this is the procurement ms a slash DPA review that we scheduled, i think we have 50 minutes, is that right?
00:08 Miguel Torres: yep that's right, we've got til about 3:50, we've got a hard blocker at 3:55 so we'll try to be crisp.
00:13 Alex Chen: Great. quick introductions, i'm alex from redwood, i'm the account lead, priya is our systems engineer who will handle most of the technical Qs. over to you, miguel, or sam?
00:22 Miguel Torres: miguel, procurement, i run vendor ops and contracting. samantha is legal and she'll lead on contract redlines. raj here is the tech lead for the AI platform.
00:31 Samantha Lee: hi all.
00:33 Priya Nair: hi, thanks, excited to get into this.
00:36 Alex Chen: Cool. agenda — high level legal asks, sla & liab caps, dpa exhibits, security artifacts (SOC2, pen test), deployment model options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), pricing approvals and onboarding steps. we can take items out if needed.
00:50 Samantha Lee: sounds good. our main priorities: data residency, KMS support, audit logs, and indemnity language — those are the big ones for us. also need to understand the sla thresholds and credit calculations.
01:04 Alex Chen: makes sense. priya, quick note: we support both hosted and private VPC modes; for regulated PHI workloads customers typically go private or our dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
01:15 Priya Nair: yup. we can run in redwood-hosted with encrypted at-rest keys managed by redwood, or we can integrate with your KMS for key wrapping. for on-prem or VPC we support customer-managed keys and we have HSM integrations for enterprise.
01:30 Raj Patel: question on logs — do you provide tenant-level audit logs and export to our SIEM? we need to keep logs for seven years for compliance.
01:39 Priya Nair: we expose audit logs and can stream to your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging sinks, retention in hosted is configurable up to X months, for extended retention we typically recommend dedicated/private where you control storage. i will follow up with the exact retention numbers and export formats.
01:52 Samantha Lee: on the dpa — can you confirm subprocessing list and whether redwood will flow down obligations to subprocessors? also need breach notification timing.
02:02 Alex Chen: standard is 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches, we can look at acceleration if required. subprocessors are listed in the DPA exhibit; we flow down relevant obligations and we can provide an updated list.
02:13 Miguel Torres: procurement is also concerned about liability caps. our policy wants a higher cap for security breaches, do you have flexibility on that?
02:21 Alex Chen: typical redwood cap is limited to fees paid in prior 12 months, with carveouts for gross negligence and willful misconduct. we can discuss specific language you need; historically we negotiate based on enterprise tier and insurance.
02:34 Samantha Lee: insurance evidence — can you send proof of cyber insurance and limits?
02:37 Alex Chen: yes, we'll attach certificate of insurance and policy summary.
02:40 Priya Nair: i'll add SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summary to the doc bundle.
02:45 Raj Patel: technical question — for the pilot we'll need to benchmark latency and token throughput. can you support a workload where we run real queries against our dataset but in a redwood sandbox?
02:55 Priya Nair: absolutely. we can run a pilot on dedicated reserved instances or in a private VPC. for ephemeral benchmarking we recommend dedicated burst capacity to mimic production throughput. i'll share the benchmark template and a sample spreadsheet.
03:06 Miguel Torres: timeline wise, procurement needs vendor questionnaire answers, po instructions, and a redlined MSA to start. we aim to finalize by mid-april for a late-april kickoff.
03:17 Alex Chen: understood. we will target sending the redlined MSA by 2025-04-01 and SOC2 artifacts by 2025-03-31.
03:22 Samantha Lee: on indemnity, we have a standard clause that we expect; does redwood accept consumer data indemnities?
03:29 Alex Chen: we have standard indemnities; specifics depend on data classification. for regulated PHI workloads we recommend private deployment and we can do additional contractual protections — we'll flag this for legal.
03:39 Raj Patel: about data residency, can we ensure data for EU customers is stored in EU regions and not replicated to US? that's a hard requirement for some products.
03:47 Priya Nair: yes, we support region pinning and can restrict replication. in hosted we have region controls; in private or dedicated you have full control. i'll include the region-residency doc.
03:58 Samantha Lee: we'd also like to understand retention deletion guarantees — if we request deletion, what's the SLA?
04:04 Alex Chen: deletion requests for customer data in hosted are processed within 30 days; for private/dedicated it's immediate as you control storage. we can include deletion certs for the pilot.
04:14 Miguel Torres: procurement has one more operational ask — we need PO templates and billing cadence, do you support monthly vs annual billing?
04:22 Alex Chen: we support both; hosted is typically monthly by usage, dedicated is usually annual commit but can do monthly invoices against the committed amount. we'll include pricing options in the worksheet.
04:31 Samantha Lee: any change logs to the DPA when you add new subprocessors? we need to be notified.
04:36 Alex Chen: yes, we notify customers of new subprocessors and update the list; there's a process in the DPA for notification windows.
04:43 Priya Nair: one note on SSO — we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, SCIM provisioning for user management, and RBAC roles you can customize.
04:52 Raj Patel: good. for the pilot we'll need can we get a self-contained test tenant with isolated model versions and KV cache cleared between runs?
04:59 Priya Nair: yep, we can spin up a dedicated tenant and provide isolation. we can also snapshot KV caches and clear them between runs.
05:08 Samantha Lee: legal exceptions — i will circulate our standard list but i foresee questions on liability cap and data processing terms.
05:15 Alex Chen: understood. let's do a quick recap of next steps to make sure we're aligned.
05:18 Miguel Torres: recap? yes please.
05:20 Alex Chen: action items: alex sends redlined MSA and pricing worksheet by 4/1; priya attaches SOC2, pen test, network diagrams by 3/31; accelera returns vendor questionnaire and PO instructions by 4/8; samantha to share exceptions list by 4/6. we'll also schedule the technical onboarding and benchmark session — priya will propose times.
05:39 Samantha Lee: sounds good, one last ask — can you include a short summary of your SLA credit calculation examples? it helps us model risk.
05:46 Alex Chen: yes, i'll include an SLA appendix showing example uptime calculations and credit percentages.
05:51 Raj Patel: if we want to request a higher liability cap for security incidents, is that done via an addendum or via the MSA redline?
05:58 Alex Chen: usually via MSA redlines and we can follow up with procurement. if it's material we'll route to legal leadership for approval.
06:05 Miguel Torres: ok, thanks all. we'll reconvene after legal has reviewed the redline, maybe 1 week after you send it.
06:12 Alex Chen: thanks everyone, appreciate it.

Notes and artifacts referenced:
- Redwood MSA draft (link shared in calendar)
- DPA exhibit and subprocessors list (will be shared)
- SOC2 Type II report (to be sent)
- Pricing worksheet and benchmark template (to be shared by AE/SE)

End of transcript.
